description: An object with a collection-like interface (`findById`, `create`, ...) that hides how an aggregate is stored.
Services and domain code do not know about SQL, ORMs or tables; they depend on the repository interface.
The code that turns rows (`created_at`, joined tables) into domain objects and back. Usually inside the repository.
A working lightweight implementation (in-memory repository) used in tests instead of the real database.
A repository that exposes query builders or ORM types, so callers depend on the storage technology anyway.
A rule enforced by storage, not only checked by the service, so concurrent requests cannot both pass the check.
